what: Glaukos makes tiny implants and drug delivery devices for eye disease: stents the width of a hair that drain fluid to lower pressure in glaucoma, and a corneal treatment for keratoconus called iLink.
customers: Ophthalmologists and surgical centres treating glaucoma and corneal disease, reimbursed by insurers and Medicare.
money: iStent implants and the iDose drug-eluting implant
moat: Surgeons trained on a specific implant and the reimbursement codes that go with it; a competing device needs its own trials, its own approval and its own billing code.
risks: Still loses money: $170M of net loss on $690M of revenue
20 times sales for a company with no profit, so the price assumes the launch keeps compounding
Medicare reimbursement decisions can change the economics of a procedure overnight
opportunities: Revenue grew from $294M to $507M in four years and is running at $690M over the last twelve months
iDose is the first drug-eluting glaucoma implant approved in the United States, a category it created
Free cash flow turned positive at $36M, the first sign the business can fund itself
watch: iDose uptake and whether its reimbursement holds at the current level.
